acceptance_evidence: Actual source review supports one observed-only whole checklist threshold and eight specific assisted workflows. The current ARM quota is 2,000, not the frozen checklist's cited 1,000; <=900 remains the explicit checklist target, not a current service-limit or 90-percent-headroom claim. Implementation and merged acceptance remain separate ledger facts.
supported_modes: Explicit AzureRM 4.50.0 raw Terraform with supplied local snapshots and optional plan; reviewed ARM 2024-05-01 and existing no-restore Bicep; saved normalized evidence and injected scoped management-plane detail reads. Complete NSG counts are observed-only; planned/declared rule arrays never establish the whole population. No new live tenant run.
positive_negative_uncertainty_tests: Exact observed custom-rule counts 0, 900, 901, 1000 and 2000; defaults excluded. Missing, malformed, duplicate, over-bound or non-Succeeded snapshots remain unknown. Bool/string counts are not integers.
Declared ARM/Bicep, raw and planned inline/separate child rules never establish complete NSG capacity. Mode must remain observed; scope completeness is not inferred from a known per-resource count.

Explicit service-endpoint counts, endpoint policy enums, bounded minimized egress/NSG summaries, gateway subnet/type references and flow-log/analytics configuration without retained destinations, names, descriptions, credentials or filter text.

Gateway-linked IPv4 prefix capacity subchecks /26, /27 and /28; missing, mixed IPv6, symbolic, inaccessible or conflicting relationships do not become capacity/segmentation passes. Conditional /26 circuit requirements remain assisted.
Canonical positive subnet/NSG links, current/stale/denied evidence, unsupported source/API versions, sensitive values, original-time replay/comparison, reports, privacy and blank owner decisions.
Preserve exact predecessor catalog bytes, original four control meanings, fixed 251 membership and every accepted per-cohort ledger receipt.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit supplied service-endpoint count, network-identifier references and private-endpoint subnet policy enum, not blanket-enable intent or effective PaaS restrictions.
evidence_requirements: Map each subnet's explicitly configured endpoint services to an approved workload need, service-side network restrictions and an accountable owner; explicit empty lists differ from missing configuration.

Distinguish classic endpoints, the current standard-service-endpoint preview and Private Link. Review any explicit network-identifier references; absence or unsupported provider fields do not establish classic mode.
Reviewer decision: are endpoints deliberately enabled only where needed, with forced-tunnel appliance bypass, service public endpoints and alternative private paths accounted for?
recommendations.limitations: Endpoint count alone cannot show approved intent or effective network restrictions. No endpoint labels, service access check, implicit provider default, network-identifier expansion or new Azure read is used.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Bounded rule-kind/action and supplied FQDN/IPv4-address counts plus private-endpoint subnet policies; no effective exfiltration verdict.
evidence_requirements: Bind the intended PaaS egress population to effective application/network rules, destinations, rule order, DNS and approved service names. Supplied counts do not validate FQDN syntax or exclusivity.

For private endpoints reconcile actual subnet network policies, routes and forward/return paths. Application rules support SNAT symmetry; network/NVA rules need appropriate SNAT. Reconcile SQL proxy/redirect limitations.

Reviewer decision: do tested attributable paths enforce the approved service destinations without IP-only or alternate-route bypass? Supply redacted evidence references, not private destination lists.
recommendations.limitations: The original relative guidance URL was resolved and inspected. No rule simulation, DNS lookup, traffic capture, log query, destination disclosure or exfiltration test is performed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Exact gateway type/subnet references with a minimum-/27 supplied-IPv4-capacity subcheck, not a whole gateway sizing verdict.
evidence_requirements: Bind each applicable gateway IP configuration to its exact subnet; do not identify a gateway by an arbitrary subnet name or infer missing relationships.
Verify at least /27 IPv4 capacity and actual deployment/circuit requirements. Current ExpressRoute guidance needs /26 or larger for 16 circuits; reconcile coexistence and other supported scenarios.
Reviewer decision: does the actual gateway subnet have adequate supported capacity for the intended topology and growth? A /27 subcheck alone cannot establish the conditional /26 requirement.
recommendations.limitations: Prefix length <=27 is a partial supplied-capacity check only. IPv6/mixed, unresolved prefixes, missing/denied subnets and unknown gateway relationships stay unknown. No circuit enumeration or subnet deployment occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Minimized custom-rule priorities/actions/directions, explicit VirtualNetwork-tag indicators and separate observed default-rule context.
evidence_requirements: Identify actual subnet/NIC NSGs and applicable custom/default rule priorities. Confirm the intended inbound isolation is not simply delegated to the default AllowVNetInBound rule.
Reconcile VirtualNetwork expansion across peering, on-premises, gateways, UDR prefixes and possible default routes; a tag is not a fixed narrow VNet CIDR.
Reviewer decision: do actual effective priorities and representative paths enforce the intended inbound boundaries, including exceptions and existing connection state?
recommendations.limitations: Observed defaults and declared custom rules are distinct; missing default configuration stays unknown. No effective-rule query, topology expansion or packet test is executed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Exact subnet/VNet inventory and attached guardrail references supporting a specific workload-owner operating-model review.
evidence_requirements: For each landing-zone subnet population identify the workload owner and approved creation/change responsibility using a redacted operating-model or change-record reference.
Reconcile platform guardrails, deny-only constraints, address allocation and controlled exceptions against actual subnet associations; PaaS subnet delegation is not ownership delegation.
Reviewer decision: can the workload owner create and operate subnets within those platform guardrails, with responsibilities explicitly accepted by the relevant humans?
recommendations.limitations: Azure resource configuration cannot attest organizational ownership or accepted responsibility. No RBAC inference, permission enumeration/change or fabricated owner confirmation is used.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Exact subnet NSG references and unique known positive NSG links with bounded minimized rule context.
evidence_requirements: Map all intended subnet and cross-landing-zone east/west boundaries to actual NSGs, NIC-level NSGs, routes and approved traffic. A positive link is not population completeness.
Review actual priority interactions: inbound subnet then NIC; outbound NIC then subnet. Include intra-subnet traffic, defaults, higher-priority exceptions and established connections.
Reviewer decision: do effective rules and attributable path evidence enforce the intended isolation across the complete applicable subnet population?
recommendations.limitations: An attached NSG or configured deny rule alone is not effective segmentation. Missing, denied, ambiguous or differently typed references remain unknown; no extra topology/NSG read is launched.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Bounded NSG rule direction/action/priority and canonical source/destination ASG references, not verified NIC membership.
evidence_requirements: Map each intended application boundary to NSG rules, actual ASG NIC membership and effective priorities. All participating ASG NICs and source/destination ASGs must satisfy same-VNet constraints.
Reconcile the architecture's central-firewall role, including conditional Virtual WAN filtering, rather than treating every central appliance as a failure.
Reviewer decision: is east/west microsegmentation enforced at the relevant subnet/NIC boundaries with demonstrated membership and intended exceptions?
recommendations.limitations: ASG references are not membership or enforcement proof. No NIC or effective-rule enumeration, appliance configuration change or packet test is performed.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: Explicit flow-log enablement, canonical target/storage/workspace IDs, analytics bool and filter-presence indicator, never ingestion.
evidence_requirements: Bind the exact enabled flow log to an intended VNet target, supported service population, compatible storage and regional Traffic Analytics workspace; an NSG target is not VNet coverage.
Supply redacted original-time ingestion, processing/freshness and operational-use references, including explicit filters, unsupported services and ExpressRoute gateway/FastPath blind spots.

Reviewer decision: are useful VNet flows actually collected and analyzed for the intended population without unsupported or duplicate NSG/VNet collection? Do not create new NSG flow logs after the documented July 2025 cutoff.
recommendations.limitations: Configured enabled flags never establish ingestion, completeness, regional support or operational usefulness. No log/data-plane/workspace query, storage read, permission change or billing access occurs.

recommendations.implemented_subclaim: For each explicit observed NSG, count the complete valid custom securityRules array from a successful 2024-05-01 detail snapshot; pass <=900 and fail >900 against the fixed checklist target, excluding defaultSecurityRules.
recommendations.method: Observed-only complete custom NSG rule count against the explicit checklist <=900 target, not the current 2,000 ARM service quota.
evidence_requirements: Require an original-time observed Succeeded detail snapshot with an explicit complete custom-rule array of at most 2,000 valid uniquely named rules and unique priorities per direction.

Evaluate exact <=900 independently of the current service quota. The current ARM table says 2,000; the frozen checklist's cited 1,000 is historical and not reused as a present quota or 90-percent-headroom claim.
Missing, malformed, symbolic, duplicate, transient, over-bound, stale or denied configuration stays unknown/error. Declared/raw/plan inline arrays do not establish all separately managed rules.
recommendations.limitations: The count is one resource's original-time explicit configuration, not estate completeness, effective rule behavior or remaining service quota. The requested 2024 Learn GET view falls back to 2026; the exact pinned 2024 Microsoft swagger is the source. No additional read or rule-list expansion occurs.
